meta.title: Install AdashimaVerse — PWA Guide
meta.description: Learn what a Progressive Web App is, what AdashimaVerse can do as a PWA, and how to install it on your phone or computer.

hero.title: Install it like an app.
hero.description: AdashimaVerse is a Progressive Web App. Add it to your home screen or desktop for a quicker, app-like way to visit the archive.

overview.title: So, what's a PWA?
overview.intro: A PWA is a website enhanced with web features that let it behave more like an installed application. There is no separate APK, EXE, or app-store download for AdashimaVerse.

cards.title: A website with an app-like shell
cards.text: It can open in its own window and launch from an icon, while the content itself remains web-based.

cards.title: Easy to access
cards.text: Put AdashimaVerse on your phone's home screen or in your computer's app launcher so the archive is one tap or click away.

cards.title: Fast repeat visits
cards.text: Your browser can keep reusable site resources cached, which can make later visits feel faster when those resources are available locally.

cards.title: No app store required
cards.text: Installation is handled by a supported browser. You do not need to find a separate AdashimaVerse listing in an app store.

whatItMeans.title: It's still the website — just packaged for easier access.

points.title: Web technology
points.text: The PWA uses the same website, URLs, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and content as the browser version.

points.title: App-like launch
points.text: Once installed, your device can give AdashimaVerse its own icon and launch surface instead of making you open a browser tab first.

points.title: Updates come from the web
points.text: There is no manual app-store update process. Changes to the site are delivered through normal web and service-worker update mechanisms.

points.title: Offline support depends on cached content
points.text: AdashimaVerse has a service worker that can cache selected site resources. Not every page or piece of content is guaranteed to work offline, especially fresh data loaded from JSON.

installation.title: Choose your device
installation.intro: The exact wording and location of the install option can vary by browser version and device.

guides.label: PHONE
guides.title: Android · Chrome
steps: Choose Install app or, on some setups, Add to Home screen.
Confirm the installation and look for the AdashimaVerse icon on your home screen or app list.
guides.tip: If Chrome offers an install prompt directly on the site, you can use that instead of opening the menu.

guides.label: DESKTOP
guides.title: Chrome · Edge
steps: Open AdashimaVerse in Chrome or Edge.
Look for an install icon in the address bar, or open the browser menu.
Select the option to Install AdashimaVerse (the wording may differ).
Confirm the installation. The PWA can then open in its own window and appear in your app list.
guides.tip: The install control may not appear until the page has finished loading and the browser decides that the site is installable.

guides.label: IPHONE / IPAD
guides.title: Safari
steps: Adjust the name if you want, then tap Add.
guides.tip: On iPhone and iPad, Safari's Add to Home Screen flow is the normal way to save a web app to the home screen.

items.title: A dedicated icon
items.text: Launch AdashimaVerse from your home screen or desktop instead of navigating to the URL each time.

items.title: A cleaner launch experience
items.text: On browsers and platforms that support standalone display, the site can open without the normal browser tab interface.

items.title: Some resources can be cached
items.text: The service worker may retain selected static resources for faster repeat visits and limited offline behavior.

items.title: Fresh content still comes from the site
items.text: News, localized JSON, and other dynamic data are deliberately fetched from the network so the archive can stay current.

items.a: It is a web app installed through your browser. It can have an app icon and an app-like launch experience, but its content is still delivered by the web.

items.q: Do I need an app store?
items.a: No. A supported browser handles the installation. There is no separate AdashimaVerse app-store package required.
Not necessarily. The service worker caches selected static resources, but fresh JSON data and other network-dependent content may still require an internet connection.

items.q: Why don't I see an Install button?
items.a: The browser controls when a native install prompt is available. If it is not shown, use your device's installation instructions above, such as Add to Home Screen on iOS.

items.q: Will installing it use more storage?
items.a: The browser may store the app shell, cached resources, and normal website data on your device. The amount varies with browser behavior and what you visit.

The website remains web-based, so new content is normally fetched from the site. Cached static files are managed by the service worker and may update when the browser installs a newer worker/cache version.
Yes. Remove the AdashimaVerse web app using your device's normal uninstall or remove-from-home-screen controls. This does not remove the website from the internet.

items.q: Is there an APK or EXE I should download?
items.a: No. Do not download a separate APK or EXE for AdashimaVerse. Use the browser installation flow described on this page.
